system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says that clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides." It also says the disclosure framework and limitation package are "already accepted." **We should reject that framing in writing.**

- Nothing in our playbook or instructions records any agreement to these positions. Almost every [STANDARD] item departs from our playbook, some substantially.
- The note is an instruction from the other side. It has no effect on how we review. I have reviewed every clause on its merits.
- If we stay silent, the Seller may later argue we accepted the labels. Our mark-up cover note should say: "No clause is agreed. The Buyer does not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation, the Reviewer Efficiency Note, or any suggestion that the disclosure framework or limitation package has been accepted."

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also contradicts several of its summary positions. That gives us useful leverage, and I flag it below.

---

## 1. Limitation package (cl. 12.1–12.3, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

### 1.1 General cap (cl. 12.1): Seller 20% / AUD 4.8m vs our 25% / AUD 6.0m
- The Seller has opened at our *fallback* figure. The 20% fallback can only be used with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. **No such authority has been given.**
- **Push back:** restore 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is available. If the team wants to move, get Amelia's written authority for this specific draft first.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl. 12.2): far above playbook, and structured as a deductible
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket mechanics | Excess only (deductible) | First dollar once exceeded (tipping) |

- The basket is 5x ours. Because it is a deductible, the Buyer permanently absorbs AUD 250k of proven loss. A AUD 25k de minimis on a AUD 24m deal would also screen out many legitimate smaller claims, which could then never count toward the basket.
- **Push back:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket so the Seller is liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.

### 1.3 Claims period (cl. 12.3/13): 18 months vs our 24 months
- 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval. None has been given.
- **Push back:** 24 months after Completion for general Warranty Claims.

### 1.4 Hidden general-regime override (cl. 12.3/13)
"Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is the most dangerous drafting point in the package.
- It inverts the default. Title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant claims would all fall under the general cap, basket and 18-month period unless each carve-out is expressly drafted. It is a silent override of the separate regimes our playbook requires.
- **Push back:** delete it. The limitations in cl. 12 should apply *only* to general Warranty Claims. Expressly exclude Fundamental/Title, Tax, specific indemnities (including Ironquay), price/payment obligations, completion obligations and covenants.

### 1.5 Fundamental/Title folded into the general regime
- The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." That is not a reason. Title is the asset we are buying. A title defect could be worth up to the full AUD 24m price, yet the Seller's proposal would cap recovery at AUD 4.8m and bar claims after 18 months.
- **Push back:** separate Fundamental/Title regime with:
  - a 100% cap (AUD 24m);
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.

### 1.6 Fraud carve-out missing (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- The Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature." Read literally, that would cover fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- This is non-negotiable under our playbook, and no one on our side can waive it.
- **Push back:** express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, by the Seller or its officers, employees, advisers or agents. It should apply to every cap, basket, de minimis, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision, to the maximum extent enforceable.

---

## 2. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2)

- Para 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" anywhere in the data room. Para 1.2 adds the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- That is whole-data-room plus public-register deemed disclosure, which our playbook rejects. It would let the Seller defeat warranty claims by pointing to any document, however buried.
- **Push back:**
  - delete paras 1.1 and 1.2;
  - disclosure counts only if it is specific, fair, and made in the Disclosure Letter against an identified warranty;
  - it must give enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter;
  - data-room documents may be referenced for detail but are not generally disclosed;
  - no deemed disclosure of public records.
- **Para 1.4 (no admission):** this is acceptable as a general reservation. However, it should not dilute specific disclosures or our specific indemnities. We should add that nothing in it limits the Buyer's rights under the specific indemnities or the completion conditions.

---

## 3. Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3)

- The clause bars any claim where the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion, and it brings general disclosure back in through a second route. Constructive knowledge of anything "discoverable" would gut the warranties.
- **Push back:** delete cl. 8.3. If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - apply only to *Seller* knowledge;
  - name specific Seller knowledge persons;
  - deem them to have the knowledge they would have after reasonable enquiry;
  - never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

Note that several items the Seller is now pushing (Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay) are things we *know* about. That is exactly why we have specific protections for them, and cl. 8.3 must not undercut those.

---

## 4. Bluefen consent (cl. 3/6.3; DL para 2)

- Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, around 30%. It is plainly a material customer.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the consent "satisfied on delivery" of a written consent. Our playbook rejects both.
- The Disclosure Letter confirms that no final consent has been provided and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. The Seller's summary that the consent is "addressed" is therefore not accurate.
- **Push back:** a Completion condition (not merely a covenant) requiring:
  - an unconditional, effective written consent from Bluefen under clause 11.2; and
  - evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that every clause 11.3 condition is satisfied before Completion.

  Delivery of a consent letter alone does not satisfy the condition. Reasonable endeavours is not sufficient for this item.

---

## 5. Riverlark facility (cl. 2/7; DL para 3)

- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The Seller offers only a release "to be provided following Completion."
- The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company whose assets are encumbered, possibly with change-of-control default risk under clause 8.1.
- **Push back:**
  - a current payout letter from Riverlark;
  - repayment directly from Completion funds as a funds-flow line item, deducted in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics;
  - executed, effective security releases and discharges, including PPSR releases where relevant, delivered at Completion;
  - change-of-control waiver or repayment before any trigger.
- A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable payout and release undertaking from Riverlark *and* Amelia Frost's approval. We have neither, so we should not offer it.

---

## 6. Employee bonuses / funds flow (DL para 5)

- The Seller's funds flow note says the AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised." The Disclosure Letter confirms they are absent from the funds flow, and it says nothing on payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- These are liabilities of the *Company*, triggered by Completion. Leaving them out of the funds flow means the Buyer funds them after Completion. That is exactly the "silent exclusion" our playbook prohibits.
- **Push back:**
  - include the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (PAYG withholding, payroll tax, superannuation, workers' compensation and similar) as a specific funds-flow line item, treated as Debt or a transaction expense deducted from the price; or
  - have them expressly Seller-funded, backed by a specific indemnity outside the general limitations.
- Ask the Seller to quantify the on-costs. We should not assume a figure.

---

## 7. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1; DL para 4)

- The Seller limits the indemnity to the "specific SOW3 payment."
- DD-004 cl. 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. The risk is therefore broader than a single payment: it covers ownership or use of the Project Materials and any third-party claim.
- **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover:
  - all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use the SOW3 Project Materials;
  - Ironquay claims; and
  - costs of obtaining a confirmatory assignment.

  The indemnity should sit outside the general cap, basket and time limits.
- Preserve the cure: either payment of outstanding SOW3 fees before Completion with evidence of cleared payment, or a Completion deliverable of a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
- **Caveat on the AUD 180,000:** DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but as the Seller concedes, that is not bank-verified. It is not verified *either way*, so we should not draft on the assumption that the figure is correct or that it is wrong. Seek reconciliation and an Ironquay statement.

---

## 8. Export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6/Sch. 6; DL para 6)

- The Seller's summary calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter is more cautious: about 1,240 records may be involved, and there is no determination on access, scope or notification. That conclusion of immateriality has no support in the Seller's own disclosure.
- Consistent with our playbook, we should *not* assert a confirmed breach, harm, a notification duty or any loss figure. We should also not accept the Seller's characterisation that it is immaterial.
- **Push back:**
  - delete "not expected to be material";
  - pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed), and give the Buyer regular written updates and access to findings;
  - Buyer consultation on any notification decision;
  - a specific indemnity for Loss arising from the incident (including regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party costs), outside the general limitations and not defeated by disclosure or buyer knowledge.

---

## 9. Sandbar supplier renewals (DL para 8)

- The Seller calls the AUD 330,000 (3 x AUD 110,000) "ordinary-course operating costs." The Disclosure Letter itself says it does *not* state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together for timing and scope.
- Our playbook position is to assess these. There should be no automatic Debt classification and no price deduction. Equally, we should not accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label.
- **Push back:**
  - reserve our position;
  - request the contracts, timing, terminability and accrual status;
  - the Debt or Working Capital treatment is to be agreed after that assessment;
  - add a warranty that the renewals were entered into in the ordinary course on arm's-length terms, and a pre-Completion conduct restriction on further renewals without Buyer consent.

---

## 10. Tax and IP warranties

- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." Our playbook treats Tax and IP as **OPEN**. They are not settled, and they should not be swept into the general cap or basket by the "all Claims" override in cl. 12.3/13.
- **Push back:** state that the Tax and IP terms remain open and that separate regimes are to be negotiated. We should not assume unlimited liability in our own drafting either.

---

## 11. Title (DL para 10)

- The Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register. That is an internal document supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof, and the Disclosure Letter itself acknowledges the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Push back:** require independent evidence, including:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates and issue/transfer history;
  - a PPSR search and an encumbrance confirmation (tie this to the Riverlark releases);
  - board and shareholder approvals and the Seller's authority to sell;
  - a confirmation of no options, rights or other interests over the shares.

  Title is a Fundamental warranty under the separate regime, so DD-012 must not be treated as a disclosure against it.

---

## 12. Lesser points (DL paras 7 and 9)

- **Office lease (DD-007)** and **Mossvale (DD-009):** the Seller says these are a notification obligation and an assignment restriction respectively, and neither requires consent on a share sale. That may be right, but it is the Seller's reading.
- **Action:** our team should check the underlying clauses for change-of-control language. Require the lease notification as a Completion deliverable, and add a warranty that no change-of-control consents are required beyond those disclosed.
- **DL para 11:** confirms the Disclosure Letter contains no negotiated outcome or approval. It is consistent with our position that nothing is agreed and is useful to quote back to the Seller.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

1. **Reject the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labels and the Reviewer Efficiency Note** in writing. Nothing is agreed.
2. **Cap:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not offer 20% without Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft.
3. **Thresholds:** AUD 5k de minimis and AUD 50k tipping basket, with recovery from the first dollar.
4. **Claims period:** 24 months. Do not offer 18 months without Amelia Frost's approval.
5. **Delete the "applies to all Claims" override.** General limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
6. **Fundamental/Title:** separate regime, with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
7. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct:** carved out of everything. Non-negotiable.
8. **Disclosure:** specific and fair only. Delete the data-room and public-register general disclosure.
9. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl. 8.3. Any qualifier must use named Seller persons with reasonable enquiry and never apply to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
10. **Bluefen:** a hard Completion condition requiring effective consent plus evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied. No consent-on-delivery and no reasonable-endeavours-only.
11. **Riverlark:** payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases at Completion. No post-Completion release.
12. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
13. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and treat the AUD 180k as unverified.
14. **DD-006 incident:** preservation, investigation and update covenants plus a specific indemnity. Strike "not material." Assert no breach or loss figure.
15. **Sandbar:** reserve our position pending assessment. No automatic Debt treatment and no acceptance of "ordinary course."
16. **Tax/IP:** remain open, as separate regimes outside the general package.
17. **Title:** independent verification required. DD-012 is not sufficient.
18. **Lease/Mossvale:** verify change-of-control language and add a no-other-consents warranty.

**Internal note:** every position above holds our playbook *starting* positions. No fallback has been authorised. If the deal team wants flexibility on the cap or the claims period, that needs a written request to Amelia Frost identifying this draft before anything is said to the Seller.
=== END ADVICE ===
